characters.note: Watson's wife, present at the breakfast opening.

characters.name: Alice Turner
characters.note: Daughter of John Turner, in love with James McCarthy.

characters.name: John Turner
characters.note: Wealthy landowner who made his money in Australia; the actual murderer.

characters.name: Charles McCarthy
characters.note: Murdered tenant farmer of Hatherley Farm, ex-Australian, former wagon-driver.

characters.name: James McCarthy
characters.note: Son of Charles McCarthy, accused of the murder.

characters.name: Patience Moran
characters.note: Fourteen-year-old daughter of the lodge-keeper, witness.

characters.name: John Cobb
characters.note: Groom who drove McCarthy senior to Ross.

locations.name: Hereford Arms, Ross

locations.name: Boscombe Pool

locations.name: Boscombe Wood

brief.era: 1880s-1890s England, with flashback to 1860s Victorian Australian goldfields.
brief.place: Rural Herefordshire near Ross; Boscombe Pool and its wooded margins; a small market town hotel; a Victorian train journey from London.
brief.dress: Victorian tweeds and travelling-cloaks for Holmes and Watson; Lestrade in light brown dustcoat and leather leggings; Holmes in a long grey travelling-cloak and close-fitting cloth cap; Turner frail, with grizzled hair and tangled beard; Alice in a respectable young woman's dress; the McCarthys in rustic working clothes; the murderer's grey cloak is a key clue.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Hatherley Farm, a two-storied slate-roofed building with lichen-stained grey walls; Boscombe Pool, a reed-girt lake; a great beech in the wood; the red jutting pinnacles of Turner's Hall above the trees; a blunt stone as weapon; a gun, an Indian cigar with holder, a pocket Petrarch; a map of Victoria.
depiction_rules: Show Holmes as a lean, gaunt, tall figure; in the tracking scene his face should show intense concentration.
Show Turner as frail and ashen with blue-tinged lips, though physically large and craggy.
The murderer is left-handed, lame in the right leg, and wears a grey cloak and thick-soled boots; keep these visible where the clues are discussed.
Do not show the murder itself; the blow is only described, so depict the aftermath or the quarrel at a distance.
Alice should be depicted as a lovely, impulsive young woman with violet eyes.
